question.text: A Credit Default Swap (CDS) buyer pays a periodic premium to the seller. What does the CDS buyer RECEIVE in the event of a default?

answer.text: A payment equal to (Notional − Recovery Value) of the underlying bond

explanation.text: The Logic: A Credit Default Swap (CDS) functions like insurance against a credit event on a reference bond. The protection buyer pays periodic premium to the seller; on a credit event, the seller compensates the buyer for the loss given default, which equals Notional × (1 − Recovery Rate), i.e., Notional minus Recovery Value. For example, on a Rs. 100 crore notional CDS with 40% recovery, the payout is Rs. 60 crore. The Trap: "Nothing" treats the contract as a lapsed insurance policy; "full notional" ignores the recovery value of the defaulted bond; "twice the premium" has no theoretical basis. Only the loss-given-default payout properly reflects CDS economics. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook supports the framing that a CDS protects the buyer against a credit event on an underlying bond and that the protection buyer pays premium to the seller like insurance, but does not explicitly state that the buyer receives Notional minus Recovery Value or present a recovery-rate-based payoff formula. The payoff formula above is general industry/regulatory CDS convention.
